["AJCR.w4-rep.datum.p1-witness","done","","DONE pic-g (0096 r5). Row consumed: the field-test vanishing IS PROVED, by pic-c's Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean at any genus-0 curve with P1 as a corollary. This row's job was to make that instantiable.

LANDED, r3: Curve/P1Curve.lean + Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean -- the three curve binders and genus = 0 at P1.asOver k over an ARBITRARY field, rooted, axiom-clean. Before r3 no AJCR object satisfied the package at all, so none of rep's ~93 consumer theorems could be instantiated at a concrete curve. That is the durable content of this row.

LANDED, r5, and DOWNGRADED after audit (I-1633): Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean is a COROLLARY LAYER, not an independent result -- all four of its declarations follow from pic-c's Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero alone, which landed 7 minutes earlier and is general in the curve. I verified the subsumption myself. The one part not duplicated is eq_of_classDeg_eq_baseChange (no Injective (classDeg) statement exists elsewhere). Also Algebra/LaurentUnits.lean: the Laurent unit group R^x x Z, with the necessity of IsDomain now a THEOREM rather than the prose assertion I first shipped (I-1634).

WITHDRAWN, r5: my r3 pricing said the remaining step needs relative Pic(P1_T) = Pic(T) x Z, 'substrate-building, not a residue'. Right about the RING case; false about the FIELD case, which closed through the chi-ledger with no relative-Pic computation at all.

SURVIVING OBLIGATION: forall k-ALGEBRA A, Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k A)), content Pic(P1_A) = Pic(A) x Z. Tracked at pic0-affine-reduction (pic-c), not here.

WHAT I KNOW ABOUT ROUTES TO IT, with the audit's correction (I-1635) applied -- I earlier called two routes FORECLOSED and only one of those clauses was audited:
* MEASURED: Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial k)) is inferInstance at a FIELD and synthInstanceFailed at a general [CommRing A], failing even when GIVEN Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A). Zero mathlib files match seminormal or traverso. So a chart-by-chart argument has no instance to stand on over a ring.
* QUOTED, NOT VERIFIED HERE: that Pic(A[t]) = Pic(A) holds EXACTLY for seminormal A is Traverso-Swan, mathematics from outside this formalization. It explains the failed instance search; it is not a formalized no-go and I should not have written it as one.
* MEASURED: subsingleton_pic0_of_affine (Pic0VanishingRoute.lean:283) runs one way and its hypothesis is vanishing of the whole picEt, which is false at P1 where a degree-one class exists."]
["AJCR.w4-rep.datum.pic0-ring-case","active","pic-c","RE-SPELLED AND SUBSTRATE BUILT; THE OBLIGATION DID NOT SHRINK (pic-c). Owner: pic-c (live, run 0106 r2); the active plus-to-Cech/Laurent comparison work is a supporting route, not a closed gate.

At genus zero, hvan and the fibrewise rigidity predicate are equivalent spellings. The rigid engine and the unit-equation lemma are genuine, sorry-free infrastructure, but hrigAff still has no producer over a general non-field test algebra. Field-point separation does not imply the affine statement.

The zero ring is not an unchecked refutation site: its antecedent is vacuous and PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton proves the conclusion there. It is therefore only a vacuous non-counterexample; inhabitability on nonempty spectra remains open.

The remaining bridge is a real degree-zero/triviality producer for arbitrary test rings (or the needed cohomology-and-base-change theorem), not a repricing of the degree condition. Do not read the supporting Cech/Laurent work as a RepresentableBy producer.

data.content:
1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianData
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Canonical cocycles of representability isomorphisms
    10	
    11	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso` is defined by Yoneda uniqueness, but mathlib does
    12	not expose the two equations that descent data consume: its universal-element intertwining
    13	formula and transitivity for three independently chosen representing objects.  These generic
    14	lemmas make those equations explicit.  In particular, the transitivity theorem proves a
    15	three-face cocycle without defining the `1,3` face as a composite.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe v u u'
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory
    23	
    24	namespace CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy
    25	
    26	/-- Transport a representation through the right adjoint of an adjunction.
    27	
    28	This is the categorical pullback step used for overlap bases: if `L ⊣ R`, then a
    29	representation of `F` by `Y` induces one of `L.op ⋙ F` by `R.obj Y`.  The statement
    30	requires only the adjunction; for schemes, `Over.mapPullbackAdj` supplies it whenever

(text: 'str', *, library: 'str', file: 'str') -> 'list[Declaration]'
def extract_declarations(text: str, *, library: str, file: str) -> list[Declaration]:
    """Parse one Lean source into declarations. Heuristic, not a real parser."""
    lines = text.splitlines()
    ns: list[str] = []
    pending_doc: str | None = None
    out: list[Declaration] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        stripped = lines[i].strip()
        if not stripped:
            i += 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("/--"):
            doc, end = _read_docstring(lines, i)
            pending_doc = doc
            i = end + 1
            continue
        if stripped.startswith("/-"):  # module/section comment — skip the block
            j = i
            while j < len(lines) and "-/" not in lines[j]:
                j += 1
            i = j + 1
            continue

        if stripped.startswith("@["):  # attribute line — keep any pending docstring
            i += 1
            continue

        m_ns = _NAMESPACE_RE.match(stripped)
        if m_ns:
            ns.append(m_ns.group(1))
            pending_doc = None
            i += 1
            continue
        m_end = _END_RE.match(stripped)
        if m_end:
            if ns and (m_end.group(1) is None or ns[-1].endswith(m_end.group(1))):
                ns.pop()
            i += 1
            continue

        m = _DECL_RE.match(stripped)
        if m:
            kind, raw_name = m.group(1), m.group(2).lstrip("@")
            qualified = ".".join([*ns, raw_name]) if raw_name else ".".join(ns)
            out.append(Declaration(
                name=qualified,
                kind=kind,
                signature=_collect_signature(lines, i),
                doc=pending_doc or "",
                library=library,
                file=file,
                line=i + 1,
            ))
            pending_doc = None
            i += 1
            continue

        pending_doc = None
        i += 1
    return out

    10	/-!
    11	# A presheaf with unique values is represented by the terminal object
    12	
    13	This file supplies the categorical bridge that was missing between "a presheaf
    14	`F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` has exactly one element at every test object" and
    15	"`F` is representable by the terminal object of `C`".
    16	
    17	Mathlib `v4.31` has `CategoryTheory.Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique` (a `C`-object
    18	`X` with `Unique (Y ⟶ X)` for every `Y` is terminal) and
    19	`CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal.ofUnique`, but **not** the presheaf-side
    20	statement: from `Nonempty (F.obj T)` and `Subsingleton (F.obj T)` at every `T`,
    21	build the natural bijection `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` that
    22	`Functor.RepresentableBy` is. Both sides of that bijection are singletons —
    23	the left because `Y` is terminal, the right by hypothesis — so the bijection
    24	and its naturality are `Subsingleton.elim`. Verified absent by search over
    25	mathlib and both projects; the nearest hits (`hasTerminal_of_unique`,
    26	`isTerminalEquivUnique`) are about representing objects, not represented
    27	presheaves.
    28	
    29	## Why it is worth a named declaration
    30	
    31	`Functor.RepresentableBy` is *data* (a chosen `Equiv` per object, plus a
    32	naturality equation), not a `Prop`. So even when a presheaf is manifestly a
    33	subterminal-and-inhabited functor, producing the `RepresentableBy` witness
    34	still requires building that `Equiv` by hand at every use site. This file does
    35	it once, at full categorical generality, so a consumer that has proved
    36	`Nonempty` and `Subsingleton` pointwise gets the representability witness by a
    37	single application — no `Equiv` plumbing.
    38	
    39	## The intended consumer
    40	
    41	`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` proves `Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))`
    42	for every `π` and test `T` (`DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero`, the empty
    43	divisor). If a lane proves the matching
    44	`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — that the empty divisor is the
    45	*only* relative effective divisor of degree `0` — then
    46	`representableByTerminal` yields
    47	`(DivFunctorDeg π 0).RepresentableBy (Over.mk (𝟙 S))` immediately, the first
    48	genuine `RepresentableBy` producer on the AJC divisor side. That `Subsingleton`
    49	is real content (a fact about `fiberDeg`, a `finrank` with a junk value at
    50	infinite dimension), and it is **not** discharged here; this file supplies only
    51	the categorical interface it plugs into.
    52	
    53	Everything here is about an arbitrary category and carries no algebraic-geometry
    54	hypothesis; nothing closes any `sorry`.
    55	-/
    56	
    57	universe w v u
    58	
    59	namespace CategoryTheory.Functor
    60	
    61	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    62	
    63	/-- **A presheaf that is pointwise nonempty and subsingleton is represented by
    64	any terminal object.**
    65	
    66	The representing map `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` sends every morphism to the
    67	unique element of `F.obj (op X)` and back to the unique morphism `X ⟶ Y` (which
    68	exists because `Y` is terminal). Both round trips, and the naturality square,
    69	are forced by the two `Subsingleton`s.
    70	
    71	This is the presheaf-side companion of `Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique`, which is
    72	absent from mathlib `v4.31`. -/
    73	noncomputable def representableByTerminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    74	    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
    75	    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
    76	    F.RepresentableBy Y where
    77	  homEquiv {X} := by
    78	    haveI := hne (Opposite.op X)
    79	    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
    80	    exact
    81	      { toFun := fun _ => Classical.arbitrary _
    82	        invFun := fun _ => hY.from X
    83	        left_inv := fun _ => hY.hom_ext _ _
    84	        right_inv := fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _ }
    85	  homEquiv_comp {X X'} f g := by
    86	    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
    87	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
    88	
    89	/-- **The `Unique`-packaged form of `representableByTerminal`.** When the values
    90	of `F` are literally `Unique` (a single default plus subsingleton), the same
    91	terminal object represents it. -/
    92	noncomputable def representableByTerminal_of_unique (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    93	    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y) (h : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Unique (F.obj T)) :
    94	    F.RepresentableBy Y :=
    95	  representableByTerminal F hY (fun T => ⟨(h T).default⟩) (fun T => (h T).instSubsingleton)
    96	
    97	/-- **Existence corollary**: a pointwise nonempty-and-subsingleton presheaf is
    98	representable (forgets the chosen terminal object). -/
    99	theorem isRepresentable_of_terminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
   100	    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
   101	    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
   102	    F.IsRepresentable :=
   103	  (representableByTerminal F hY hne hss).isRepresentable
   104	
   105	end CategoryTheory.Functor

     9	/-!
    10	# The empty divisor: the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily`
    11	
    12	`Scheme.DivFamily π T` (`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`) is the carrier of the whole
    13	divisor side of the Milne–Kollár campaign: `Scheme.DivFunctor`, its degree slices
    14	`Scheme.DivFunctorDeg`, the Abel maps `abelDeg` / `abelMapWitness`, the flatness
    15	inputs of `Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean`, and `IdentityComponent`'s
    16	`ClassDegreePinned` acceptance test are all quantified over it. Until this file it
    17	had **zero producers**, for any `π`, any base, and any test object including the
    18	trivial one — measured with `exact?` and recorded in its own docstring. The
    19	consequence recorded there: *every* statement quantified over a `DivFamily` was
    20	"true but untested", with no instance to be wrong about.
    21	
    22	This file supplies the first inhabitant, unconditionally in `π : X ⟶ S` and
    23	`T : Over S`: the **empty divisor** `D = ∅`, whose structure sheaf `O_D` is the
    24	zero module and whose ideal is all of `O_{X_T}`.
    25	
    26	## Why the empty divisor satisfies the divisor condition
    27	
    28	The divisor condition of `DivFamily` is that the kernel ideal `I = ker q` be
    29	*invertible* (`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`). For `q : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0` the kernel is
    30	`O_{X_T}` itself (`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`), and the structure sheaf is
    31	trivially locally trivial (`Scheme.PicSharp.isLocallyTrivial_unit`, restated here as
    32	`isLocallyTrivial_unit'` because that one is `private`). So the invertible-ideal
    33	condition — the field that makes `DivFamily` a divisor rather than an arbitrary
    34	quotient — holds *for the reason it should*: `O_{X_T}/O_{X_T} = 0` cuts out the
    35	empty subscheme, an effective divisor of degree zero.
    36	
    37	The three remaining fields are properties of the zero module, and the file proves
    38	each rather than assuming it:
    39	
    40	* `isFinitePresentation` — the zero module is finitely presented. Mathlib has no
    41	  instance for this (measured: `infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
    42	  `(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so §1 builds the `QuasicoherentData`:
    43	  the singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site
    44	  (`coversTop_singleton_top`), the restriction functor preserves zero objects
    45	  (`preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`, proved from `PresheafOfModules` extensionality
    46	  because instance search for it times out), and a zero sheaf of modules has an
    47	  *empty* presentation — no generators and no relations, both trivially finite.
    48	* `flat` — flatness over the base. The section modules of a zero module are
    49	  subsingletons, and a subsingleton module is flat.
    50	* `properSupport` — the schematic support of the zero module is the subscheme cut
    51	  out by the annihilator, which is `⊤`, so the support is **empty**
    52	  (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.instIsEmptyCarrierCarrierCommRingCatSubschemeTop`) and any
    53	  morphism out of it is proper via `IsProper.instOfIsFinite`. It is free here for that
    54	  reason, and in particular with **no properness assumption on `π`**. (An earlier
    55	  revision added "and it is a real hypothesis for a nonempty divisor". That half was
    56	  never measured — nothing here or elsewhere in the project exhibits a divisor where
    57	  `properSupport` fails or is expensive, and `DivFunctorDef.lean` says it is *automatic*
    58	  when `π` is proper. Dropped rather than repaired: the free-here half is what this
    59	  file establishes.)
    60	
    61	## What this does and does not buy
    62	
    63	**Does**: the divisor cluster is no longer vacuous. `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)` for
    64	every `π` and `T`; `(DivFunctor π).obj (op T)` and `(DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T)`
    65	are inhabited; `HasFiberDeg zero 0`; and the base-change action carries `zero` to
    66	`zero` (`pullbackAlong_zero`), so the classes are a global section of `DivFunctor`
    67	rather than a fibrewise accident. Every theorem in `DivDegree.lean` and
    68	`DivPushforwardFlat.lean` now has a witness to be checked against.
    69	
    70	**Does not**: this closes no `sorry` and witnesses no antecedent of
    71	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`. In particular it is *not* a step of D1′: the
    72	campaign's D1′ wants divisor families of a **prescribed positive degree** `d`
    73	arising from a very ample `O(1)`, which needs the projectivity input
    74	(`AJC.picrep.projectivity`) and P5 uniform `H¹` vanishing. What the empty divisor
    75	does for that programme is remove the possibility that the target type is
    76	uninhabited — a question that had to be settled before any positive-degree producer
    77	could be believed, and which no lane had settled in either direction.
    78	
    79	**One caveat, stated because it is the natural over-reading.** The degree-zero slice
    80	being inhabited does *not* make `DivFunctorDeg π 0` representable by the terminal
    81	object `Over.mk (𝟙 S)`. That would need the slice to be a *singleton* at every test
    82	object, and this file proves only the `Nonempty` half. The missing half is
    83	`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — i.e. that the empty divisor is the
    84	*only* relative divisor of degree `0`. That is the expected statement (a degree-`0`
    85	effective divisor on a fibre of a relative curve is empty), but it is a fact about
    86	`fiberDeg`, not a formality: `fiberDeg` is a `finrank` with a junk value at
    87	infinite dimension. Neither direction is proved here.
    88	
    89	**Corrected, and the correction is the useful part** (fresh-context audit of this file,
    90	2026-07-30). An earlier revision of this paragraph said "no lane holds it". That is
    91	FALSE: the analogous `Subsingleton` *is* landed, hours earlier, on the **sibling**
    92	project's carrier — `instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero`
    93	(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean`) and, over an arbitrary test ring,
    94	`instSubsingletonDivFamZarZeroGeneral` plus a full `RepresentableBy` producer
    95	(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroRep.lean`).
    96	
    97	What survives, for a **sharper** reason than the carrier mismatch: their proof is not
    98	portable because it never passes through a `finrank` at all. It runs on `IsCertified`
    99	and `rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton` over `Away` localisations of section rings,
   100	machinery that exists only on the Zariski-certified carrier `DivFamZar : Type u`. AJC's
   101	`fiberDeg` is a `Module.finrank` of fibre sections. So the honest statement is: nobody
   102	holds it *for `Scheme.DivFamily`*, and the sibling's landed route does not transport.
   103	Their success is also evidence *against* this paragraph's own framing — it shows
   104	degree-zero uniqueness can be reached without any finiteness-of-sections argument on a
   105	suitable carrier, so "needs finiteness of the fibre sections" is a claim about AJC's
   106	chosen `fiberDeg`, not about the mathematics. The row `AJC.picrep.divzero` records it as
   107	the open question this file leaves.
   108	
   109	## Main declarations
   110	
   111	* `Scheme.DivFamily.zero π T` — the empty divisor family.
   112	* `Scheme.DivFamily.instNonempty` — `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)`, as an instance.
   113	* `Scheme.DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero` — base change carries `zero` to `zero`.
   114	* `Scheme.DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero` / `hasFiberDeg_zero` — the empty divisor has
   115	  fibre degree `0` at every point.
   116	* `Scheme.DivFunctor.zeroClass` / `Scheme.DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass` — the resulting
   117	  inhabitants of the functor and of its degree-`0` slice, with
   118	  `Scheme.DivFunctor.map_zeroClass` making the first a global section.
   119	* `Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_isZero` — reusable: a zero sheaf of
   120	  modules on any scheme is finitely presented. Absent from Mathlib.
   121	* `Scheme.Modules.coversTop_singleton_top`,
   122	  `Scheme.Modules.preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`,
   123	  `Scheme.Modules.isZero_free_pempty` — the other reusable bricks §1 needed.
   124	
   125	Every declaration here is `sorry`-free and axiom-clean
   126	(`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`), measured against
   127	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` reporting `sorryAx` in the same probe file with the
   128	oleans rebuilt first.
   129	
   130	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:red`/`df:div`, Ex. `ex:DivC`
   131	(arXiv:math/0504020).
   132	-/

RE-READING HEAD AT COMMIT TIME MAKES THE GUARD'S COMPARE-AND-SWAP PASS VACUOUSLY, AND THE PRIVATE INDEX DOES NOT COVER THIS

MEASURED (janitor, pic-e 0095 r6, commit 3a511854e3). I ran the full I-1222 route -- fresh private index, read-tree HEAD, add only my 10 explicit paths, verified `diff --cached --name-status` listed exactly those 10, zero deletions. The commit still reverted another lane's file (`fc6de4ab54`, landed in the ~90s between my read-tree and my commit).

THE BUG IS ONE SHELL IDIOM. I set the guard's variable as `export ARCHON_COMMIT_BASE=$("$HORIZON_GIT" rev-parse HEAD)` **in the commit step**, i.e. re-read HEAD instead of reusing the sha the index was seeded from. The hook then compares HEAD to itself and always passes. The guard is the only mechanism that catches a mid-pass HEAD advance -- the private index cannot, because read-tree snapshots a tree and a later commit is invisible to it. Capture BASE once, before read-tree, and reuse that literal.

WHY IT LOOKED FINE: 10 staged paths, 10 verified, and the commit itself printed "11 files changed". Only reading EVERY path of the post-commit `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` caught the 11th. That is the check I-1222 demands and the one that earned its keep here.

Damage was nil (both edits whitespace-only; I normalized the YAML across all three shas and the content is identical, and the owning lane then re-landed their wrapping as 73e93c577c). The lesson is the idiom, not the outcome.

   926	  \(\rho_S\) and \(\gamma_S\) (\ref{thm:divClassifyZar}) are mutually inverse bijections

   936	  \(v\) by hypothesis, and by the uniqueness clause of \ref{thm:divClassifyZar} any
   937	  morphism classifying a class \emph{is} the classifying morphism of that class; hence

     8	/-!
     9	# The Abel-source interface: properness and irreducibility of the Jacobian
    10	(Wave-5 D3, routes P-B / GI-(a))
    11	
    12	`AbelSourceData d` packages a proper, geometrically irreducible source scheme `D` over
    13	`k` together with an *Abel morphism* `abel : D ⟶ d.J` into the representing object of
    14	the Jacobian datum whose underlying scheme map is surjective.  Two of the three frozen
    15	Wave-5 targets are theorems **conditional on this interface** (w5-worksheet §1 D3):
    16	
    17	* `universallyClosed_of_abelSource` (**P2**): `UniversallyClosed d.J.hom` — `d.J` is
    18	  the image of the proper source: `abel.left ≫ d.J.hom = D.hom` (`Over.w`) is
    19	  universally closed and `abel.left` is surjective, so mathlib's
    20	  `UniversallyClosed.of_comp_surjective` applies.
    21	* `isProper_of_abelSource` (**P3**): `IsProper d.J.hom` — assembly of X1
    22	  separatedness (`JacobianData.isSeparated`), P2, and the datum's
    23	  `locallyOfFiniteType` certificate (quasi-compactness is implied, `UC → QC`).
    24	* `geometricallyIrreducible_of_abelSource` (**G1**, route GI-(a)): for every field
    25	  `K/k` the base change `D_K` is irreducible (the certificate), the base-changed Abel
    26	  morphism `D_K ⟶ J_K` is surjective (`Surjective` is stable under base change), and
    27	  a continuous surjective image of an irreducible space is irreducible
    28	  (`Function.Surjective.irreducibleSpace`) — so `J_K` is irreducible, uniformly in
    29	  `K`, which is exactly the `geometrically` quantifier.
    30	
    31	## Design decisions recorded (the interface spelling)
    32	
    33	* **Geometric-irreducibility certificate.**  `GeometricallyIrreducible D.hom` alone:
    34	  G1 consumes exactly per-`K` irreducibility of `D_K`, and neither P2 nor P3 consumes
    35	  reducedness — so no `GeometricallyReduced`/`GeometricallyIntegral` field is carried.
    36	  (The eventual producer has integrality available anyway and mathlib's
    37	  `GeometricallyIntegral → GeometricallyIrreducible` instance bridges,
    38	  `Geometrically/Integral.lean`.)
    39	* **Surjectivity certificate.**  The single field `Surjective abel.left` (mathlib's
    40	  topological surjectivity class) suffices for BOTH consumers.  Probe result: the
    41	  pinned mathlib has `MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange @Surjective`
    42	  (`AlgebraicGeometry/PullbackCarrier.lean:431`), so surjectivity base-changes to
    43	  every field `K/k` — no `∀ K`-quantified field is needed.
    44	* **Topology bridge.**  The "continuous surjective image of an irreducible space is
    45	  irreducible" brick anticipated by the recon (§3.3) already exists in the pinned
    46	  mathlib: `Function.Surjective.irreducibleSpace` (`Topology/Irreducible.lean:540`).
    47	  No project-side topology infrastructure is required.
    48	
    49	## The P1 discharge route (recorded for the GATED producer; do NOT build here)
    50	
    51	No instance of `AbelSourceData` is constructed in this file — the producer (brick P1)
    52	is gated on the DD lanes' shapes freezing (w5-worksheet §1 D3).  Its recorded route:
    53	
    54	* `D` := the proper degree-`n` divisor scheme (`Div^n`, `n ≥ genus C`) from the
    55	  DD-Q/DD-R quasi-projectivity campaign; `isProper` from that construction;
    56	  `geometricallyIrreducible` from geometric integrality of `C^n_K` (iterated
    57	  `isIntegral_tensorObj_left`, `AbelianVariety/Rigidity.lean:160`, over the landed
    58	  `Curve/BaseChangeInstances.lean` stack) pushed to `Div^n` along the quotient/chart
    59	  presentation.
    60	* `abel` := `d.rep.homEquiv.symm` (through `JacobianData.homEquiv`) of the universal
    61	  degree-`n` divisor-family class shifted into `pic0Subgroup` by the `fiberTwist`
    62	  degree shifter (`RiemannRoch/FiberTwist.lean:301`, `classDeg_fiberTwist :393` — no
    63	  rational point needed).
    64	* `surjective` := field-point coverage from `riemann_inequality_curve`
    65	  (`RiemannRoch/ChiCurve.lean:183`): for every point of `d.J.left`, its residue-field
    66	  point is a degree-0 class `λ` on `C_K`; the `fiberTwist` shift makes it degree
    67	  `n ≥ genus C`, so `h⁰ ≥ deg + 1 - genus C ≥ 1` produces an effective representative,
    68	  i.e. a `Div^n`-point over (an extension of) `K` hitting the given point — hence
    69	  `Function.Surjective abel.left` on topological points.
    70	-/

    75	universe u
    76	
    77	open CategoryTheory Limits
    78	
    79	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    80	
    81	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    82	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    83	
    84	/-- **The Abel-source interface** (Wave-5 D3, one substrate for routes P-B and
    85	GI-(a)): a proper, geometrically irreducible scheme over `k` mapping onto the
    86	representing object of the Jacobian datum `d`.  Produced once by the gated brick P1
    87	(proper `Div^n` + Abel morphism via `d.rep.homEquiv.symm` + `fiberTwist` shift +
    88	`riemann_inequality_curve` coverage — see the file docstring); consumed by the
    89	conditional theorems P2/P3/G1 below.  NEVER a sorried instance. -/
    90	structure AbelSourceData (d : JacobianData C) : Type (u + 1) where
    91	  /-- The source scheme over `k` (the proper divisor scheme `Div^n`-to-be). -/
    92	  D : Over (Spec (.of k))
    93	  /-- Properness certificate for the source (from the `Div^n` construction). -/
    94	  isProper : IsProper D.hom
    95	  /-- Geometric-irreducibility certificate for the source: `D_K` is irreducible for
    96	  every field `K/k`.  This is all G1 consumes; the producer may derive it from
    97	  geometric integrality via mathlib's bridge instance. -/
    98	  geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible D.hom
    99	  /-- The Abel morphism, over `Spec k`. -/
   100	  abel : D ⟶ d.J
   101	  /-- Surjectivity certificate on underlying schemes.  Mathlib's `Surjective` class
   102	  is stable under base change, so this single field base-changes to every field
   103	  `K/k` (no `∀ K` quantifier needed). -/
   104	  surjective : Surjective abel.left
   105	
   106	variable {d : JacobianData C}
   107	
   108	/-- **P2 (Wave-5 target 2, universal closedness; route P-B)**: the structure morphism
   109	of the representing object of a Jacobian datum is universally closed, given any Abel
   110	source.  Milne's completeness step: `abel.left ≫ d.J.hom = a.D.hom` (`Over.w`) is
   111	universally closed since `a.D` is proper, and `abel.left` is surjective, so
   112	`UniversallyClosed.of_comp_surjective` applies. -/
   113	theorem universallyClosed_of_abelSource (a : AbelSourceData d) :
   114	    UniversallyClosed d.J.hom := by
   115	  haveI : UniversallyClosed (a.abel.left ≫ d.J.hom) := by
   116	    rw [Over.w a.abel]
   117	    exact a.isProper.toUniversallyClosed
   118	  haveI : Surjective a.abel.left := a.surjective
   119	  exact UniversallyClosed.of_comp_surjective a.abel.left d.J.hom
   120	
   121	/-- **P3 (Wave-5 target 2, properness assembly)**: the representing object of a
   122	Jacobian datum is proper over `k`, given any Abel source.  Assembly of the three
   123	`IsProper` constituents: separatedness is X1 (`JacobianData.isSeparated`, group-
   124	theoretic), universal closedness is P2, local finite-typeness is the datum's
   125	construction certificate; quasi-compactness is implied (`UC → QC`). -/
   126	theorem isProper_of_abelSource (a : AbelSourceData d) : IsProper d.J.hom :=
   127	  haveI : IsSeparated d.J.hom := d.isSeparated
   128	  haveI : UniversallyClosed d.J.hom := universallyClosed_of_abelSource a
   129	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType d.J.hom := d.locallyOfFiniteType
   130	  ⟨⟩
   131	
   132	/-- **G1 (Wave-5 target 3, geometric irreducibility; route GI-(a))**: the structure
   133	morphism of the representing object of a Jacobian datum is geometrically irreducible,
   134	given any Abel source.  For each field `K/k` and each pullback `Z` of `d.J.hom` along
   135	`y : Spec K ⟶ Spec k`: the base-changed source `D_K` is irreducible (the
   136	certificate), the comparison morphism `D_K ⟶ Z` induced by `abel` is the base change
   137	of `abel.left` along `Z ⟶ d.J.left` (pullback pasting), hence surjective, and the
   138	continuous surjective image of an irreducible space is irreducible. -/
   139	theorem geometricallyIrreducible_of_abelSource (a : AbelSourceData d) :
   140	    GeometricallyIrreducible d.J.hom := by
   141	  constructor
   142	  intro K _ y Z fst snd h
   143	  -- the base-changed source `D_K` is irreducible
   144	  haveI : IrreducibleSpace ↥(pullback a.D.hom y) :=
   145	    a.geometricallyIrreducible.geometrically_irreducibleSpace y
   146	      (pullback.fst a.D.hom y) (pullback.snd a.D.hom y)
   147	      (IsPullback.of_hasPullback a.D.hom y)
   148	  -- `D_K` is also the pullback of the composite `abel.left ≫ d.J.hom` along `y`
   149	  have s : IsPullback (pullback.fst a.D.hom y) (pullback.snd a.D.hom y)
   150	      (a.abel.left ≫ d.J.hom) y := by

    10	/-!
    11	# The widened `DivFamZar` (R2, human decision I-0492)
    12	
    13	The endpoint of the widening.  `IsLocallyCertifiedAff` is the locally-certified predicate
    14	whose local certificates are carried by **arbitrary affine-open covers** rather than by basic
    15	opens of a fixed pair of pinned `P¹` charts, and `DivFamZarAff` is its `DivEq` quotient —
    16	the object the human decision of 2026-07-28 is about.
    17	
    18	## Why this is strictly weaker than the old predicate, which is the whole point
    19	
    20	`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) turns every old cover datum into
    21	a widened one, and `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean` migrates the CERTIFICATE on top of it, so
    22	`isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` holds: anything the old
    23	predicate certified, the new one certifies.  The converse fails, and its failure is exactly
    24	the content of R2 — a divisor straddling both pinned vertical fibres has no chart-typed
    25	certificate (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 4 §4.3, on-stratum witness at every `g ≥ 2`)
    26	but does admit an affine-open one, because `supp D` is finite over `R` and therefore lies in a
    27	single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`).
    28	
    29	So `DivFamZarAff` is the value on which the divisor functor can be a Zariski sheaf over an
    30	ARBITRARY field, with no `|P¹(k)| ≥ n + 2` hypothesis anywhere — the field-uniform fix.
    31	
    32	## The two relocated obligations (I-0492 clause 4)
    33	
    34	* **(i) fibrewise-finite support.** NOT a field of anything here.  It is not implied by
    35	  what a `LocalEquations` carries (`d.eqn ≡ r` for a non-unit `r ∈ R` is germ-regular with a
    36	  whole fibre curve in its support), so it must come from the seed's own degree data.  It
    37	  enters as an explicit hypothesis at the point of use, never as carrier data: concretely as
    38	  the `hfib` argument of `AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy`
    39	  (`DivisorFamilyAffAssemble.lean`) and as `AffCoverData.SwallowedBy`
    40	  (`DivisorFamilyAffSwallow.lean`).  Neither is a field of anything in this file.
    41	* **(ii) what the fixed-pair confinement was silently supplying.** Discharged in
    42	  `DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean` (`exists_mem_pieces` from the joint cover,
    43	  `flat_sections_pieces` from the flat structure morphism) and in
    44	  `DivisorFamilyAffPerPiece.lean` (the whole per-piece layer, from openness and affineness).
    45	
    46	## Main declarations
    47	
    48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff` — a certified family over a widened cover.
    49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertifiedAff` — the widened locally-certified predicate.
    50	* `IsLocallyCertifiedAff.of_divEq` — it respects divisor equality.
    51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff` — the widened functor value, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`
    52	  and `picClass`.
    53	
    54	The comparison with the chart-typed predicate — `isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified`
    55	and `DivFamZar.toAff` — is in `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean`, which imports this file.
    56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the pointwise gate,
    57	  one base point at a time, over the widened predicate.
    58	-/

    61	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    62	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    63	
    64	universe u
    65	
    66	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
    67	
    68	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    69	
    70	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    71	
    72	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    73	  [Algebra k R]
    74	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
    75	
    76	/-! ## Certified families over a widened cover -/
    77	
    78	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over a widened cover**: a local-equation
    79	system, an affine-open cover datum, an adaptation, and the certificate.  The cover is part of
    80	the data (it is chosen per family), exactly as the old `adaptation` field bundled its own
    81	`FinCoverData`. -/
    82	structure CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff (n : ℕ) : Type u where
    83	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
    84	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
    85	  /-- The affine-open cover carrying the certificate. -/
    86	  cover : AffCoverData C R
    87	  /-- The adaptation of the system to that cover. -/
    88	  adaptation : AffAdaptation cover eqns
    89	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
    90	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
    91	
    92	/-! ## The widened locally-certified predicate -/
    93	
    94	variable {C R}
    95	
    96	/-- **The widened locally-certified pin.**  Identical in shape to `IsLocallyCertified`
    97	(`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`) — a span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R` with certified families over
    98	the away localizations, divisor-equal to the pulled system — except that the local
    99	certificates live over ARBITRARY AFFINE-OPEN covers.
   100	
   101	The base-side structure is untouched on purpose: R2 widens where the pieces live on the
   102	CURVE, and changes nothing about the Zariski cover of the base. -/
   103	def IsLocallyCertifiedAff (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
   104	  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
   105	    ∀ i : Fin m,
   106	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
   107	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
   108	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away (g i)) n,
   109	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
   110	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
   111	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   112	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))
   113	
   114	/-- **The widened pin respects divisor equality** — the local `DivEq`s transport through
   115	`divEq_pullback`, verbatim as in the chart-typed case. -/
   116	theorem IsLocallyCertifiedAff.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   117	    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
   118	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d' := by
   119	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
   120	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
   121	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
   122	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
   123	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
   124	  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
   125	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
   126	      h _ _)⟩
   127	
   128	/-! ## The comparison with the chart-typed predicate
   129	
   130	`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) already migrates the COVER
   131	sorry-free, and the adaptation's equations and `eqn_rel` transport with it because the pieces
   132	are literally the same opens, only reindexed along `finSumFinEquiv`.
   133	
   134	The migration of the CERTIFICATE is landed too, in `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean`
   135	(`DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_toAff`, all seven clauses).  Clauses (c1) are `rfl` at the
   136	relabelled index; the glued clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transport along `LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft`
   137	in its `symm` direction, which evaluates cast-free, so the intertwining with
   138	`deltaLeft`/`deltaRight` is componentwise and `Module.rankAtStalk` invariance is
   139	`rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv`.  No clause changes, only the index does.
   140	
   141	A predecessor docstring here estimated that transport at about a hundred lines of equalizer
   142	bookkeeping.  That was wrong by an order of magnitude and the reason generalises: arrange the
   143	reindexed cover so its pieces are DEFINITIONALLY the original pieces at the relabelled index,
   144	and the overlap data at `(i, j)` becomes `rfl`-equal to the original at `(e i, e j)`, because
   145	reindexing acts diagonally on the pair index.  Then no intertwining lemma exists to prove. -/
   146	
   147	/-! ## The widened functor value -/
   148	
   149	variable (C R) (n : ℕ)
   150	
   151	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on widened locally-certified systems. -/
   152	def divFamZarAffSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
   153	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d} where
   154	  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
   155	  iseqv :=
   156	    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,
   157	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
   158	
   159	/-- **The widened divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (R2, I-0492): locally
   160	certified systems of degree `n` up to divisor equality, where "certified" is now witnessed by
   161	arbitrary affine-open covers of the relative curve.
   162	
   163	This is the carrier that is field-uniform: no hypothesis on `|P¹(k)|` appears anywhere in its
   164	definition or in the per-piece layer that produces it. -/
   165	def DivFamZarAff : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarAffSetoid C R n)
   166	
   167	namespace DivFamZarAff
   168	
   169	variable {C R n}
   170	
   171	/-- The class of a widened locally certified system. -/
   172	def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) :
   173	    DivFamZarAff C R n :=
   174	  Quotient.mk (divFamZarAffSetoid C R n) ⟨d, hd⟩
   175	
   176	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   177	    {h₁ : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d₁} {h₂ : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d₂} :
   178	    mk d₁ h₁ = mk d₂ h₂ ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ :=
   179	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamZarAffSetoid C R n)
   180	
   181	/-- **The Picard class of a widened divisor class** `𝒪(D)`, well defined by
   182	`picClass_eq_of_divEq`.  This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes, unchanged by the widening. -/
   183	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFamZarAff C R n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
   184	  Quotient.lift
   185	    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d} =>
   186	      d.1.picClass)
   187	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
   188	
   189	@[simp]
   190	lemma picClass_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
   191	    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) : picClass (mk d hd) = d.picClass :=
   192	  rfl
   193	
   194	end DivFamZarAff
   195	
   196	/-! ## The pointwise gate over the widened predicate -/
   197	
   198	variable {C R n}
   199	
   200	/-- **The pointwise certificate gate, widened.** If over every prime of the base there is an
   201	away localization carrying a widened certified family divisor-equal to the pulled system, the
   202	system is widened-locally certified.  Same quasi-compactness step as
   203	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` (`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`): the good
   204	elements' basic opens cover `Spec R`, so finitely many span the unit ideal.
   205	
   206	This is the shape the geometry produces — the support tube isolates pieces over a
   207	neighbourhood of ONE base point, and every fibre analysis reads at a single prime. -/
   208	theorem isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_exists_away
   209	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   210	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   211	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
   212	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
   213	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away r) n,
   214	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
   215	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
   216	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   217	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) :
   218	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d := by
   219	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hgood⟩ := exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime
   220	    (fun r =>
   221	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
   222	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
   223	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away r) n,
   224	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
   225	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
   226	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   227	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) h
   228	  exact ⟨m, g, hg, hgood⟩
   229

     9	/-!
    10	# The Σ-chart over the R2 carrier: the widened Abel chart reaches the seam
    11	
    12	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffClassDegree.lean` discharges `hdegAff`, so the widened chart value is
    13	a degree-zero class with no hypothesis beyond the chart-index constraint.  **This file spends
    14	that**: the widened analogues of `chartValueTrans` and `abelSigmaChart`
    15	(`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:174/205`), which take the R2 carrier mandated by human
    16	decision `I-0492` all the way to the input type of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.
    17	
    18	## What this closes, and it is a carrier-target gap rather than a lemma
    19	
    20	Memory `census-the-carrier-target-pair` records the defect this repairs: a replaced carrier can

   442	\begin{theorem}[Regularity of the pulled equations of a locally certified system]
   443	  \label{thm:isLocallyCertified_pullback_regular}
   444	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors}
   445	  \uses{def:isLocallyCertified, def:localEquations_pullback, def:relCurveMap}
   446	  \leanok
   447	  Let \(d\) be locally certified of degree \(n\) over \(R\), and let \(R \to R'\) be an
   448	  arbitrary morphism of \(k\)-algebras. Then the equations of \(d\) pulled back along
   449	  \(C_{R'} \to C_R\) are regular; hence the pullback \(d|_{R'}\) is again a local-equation
   450	  system (\ref{def:localEquations_pullback}), with no flatness hypothesis on \(R \to R'\).
   451	\end{theorem}
   452	\begin{proof}
   453	  \leanok
   454	  Regularity of a section is a condition on its germ at each point, hence may be checked on
   455	  any open cover of \(C_{R'}\). Let \(g_1,\dots,g_m\) be the unit-ideal family certifying
   456	  \(d\). Their images \(\varphi(g_i) \in R'\) again generate the unit ideal, so the open
   457	  immersions \(C_{R'_{\varphi(g_i)}} \to C_{R'}\) cover \(C_{R'}\); it suffices to prove
   458	  regularity of the pulled germs at points of each such chart.
   459	
   460	  Fix \(i\). The localisation map factors: \(R \to R_{g_i} \to R'_{\varphi(g_i)}\), the
   461	  second arrow being the induced map of away localisations. Correspondingly
   462	  \[
   463	    C_{R'_{\varphi(g_i)}} \longrightarrow C_{R_{g_i}} \longrightarrow C_R
   464	  \]
   465	  composes to the restriction of \(C_{R'} \to C_R\), so the pulled equations over
   466	  \(R'_{\varphi(g_i)}\) are the equations of \(d\) pulled first to \(C_{R_{g_i}}\) and then
   467	  along the second arrow. On \(C_{R_{g_i}}\) the pulled system is divisor-equal to the
   468	  local-equation system of a \emph{certified} family \(G_i\) by hypothesis. For a certified
   469	  family the pulled equations along an arbitrary base change are regular: clause (c1) of
   470	  the certificate makes each chart colength module projective, so the multiplication-by-
   471	  \(f_j\) sequence \(0 \to \struct{}(P_j) \to \struct{}(P_j) \to Q_j \to 0\) is split as
   472	  \(R\)-modules and stays exact after \(- \otimes_R R'\), which is precisely the statement
   473	  that the pulled equation is again a nonzerodivisor. Finally, divisor equality is
   474	  preserved by pullback and units pull back to units, so regularity transports from the
   475	  pulled equations of \(G_i\) to those of \(d\).
